fix(net): fix double encoding issue

The uri.setQuery() method takes an argument for whether or not to decode that was not being used.
Because of this fix, BaseServerModifier is no longer necessary (although the API for configuring it
has been left the same to avoid breaking its usage).

BREAKING CHANGE: UrlModifier now avoids doubly encoding the query string. Any steps taken on the
receiving end of these requests to code around that bug need to be reviewed and possibly removed.

BREAKING CHANGE: os.net.BaseServerExpression was removed because it was not fully featured for
parsing out domain names. Please use `new goog.Uri(str).getDomain() or `new URL(str).hostname`
instead.

message:
fix(query): Only layers affected by entry changes should load

Previously, using a double-wildcard area to load features from multiple layers and then going into

one of those layers' filter GUIs to add an attribute filter would cause both layers to load on

Apply. Now, rather than merging the entries and always removing all and adding back in the merged

entries, we just remove the entries for the layerIds affected by the incoming entries. For the merge

case, the old entries for the revert are filtered from the full set. The non-merge case (all layer

advanced view) still removes/adds all.

author: Mike Roth <Michael.Roth@caci.com>
message:
feat(search): added text transform capability to search input
Added a directive and text transformers to transform input text. Transformers are registered with a manager via a plugin.
Search indexing will disregard punctuation that it doesn't recognize. Text copied from a word processing application may have smart quotes, which will be disregarded by a search analyzer while the actual intent is the treat the quoted text as a search phrase. The result is that each symbol is considered independently and the results are a union instead of being treated as a phrase. Adding the text-transform attribute to an input, and optionally, specifying a comma-separated list of transformers to text-transform-options to apply, provides a mechanism to prevent these cases by applying text transforms to the input text.

UUOM-435

keeping a single instance of the shape with a white fill, using the

mixin loaded by the Cesium plugin which could disable that since the
billboards no longer need the original image style off of those.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
refactor(cesium): reorganize featureconverter

This is largely a reorganization, not a rewrite or a change in logic.
FeatureConverter was a spaghetti mess and hard to make sense of for
anyone outside of a couple of experts.

The general design for the refactor is shown in sync/convertertypes.js
and sync/runconverter.js. The individual converter implementations are
all pulled in by sync/converter.js.

This is largely an attempt at feature-parity with the previous
converter, with the following changes:

  - Several style bugs were fixed by consolidating and reusing
    style code where possible instead of using the previous one-off
    implementations
  - All functions being sent a feature, geometry, style, and context now
    have a consistent parameter order everywhere
  - A few minor performance items were added (typically things like
    using scratch arrays objects where possible)
  - All instances of @suppress {checkTypes} were removed and fixed
  - Most larger functions have been split into smaller blocks with a
    couple of exceptions.

I attempted to change anything outside of FeatureConverter the least
amount possible (VectorSynchronizer and VectorContext) other than
converting them to ES6 class syntax.

FeatureConverter was previously entirely missing tests. WebGL mocks
have been added and are fleshed out engouh that we can use a real
Cesium scene in the tests. Many tests have been added but I still have
more to write.

Note that the tests currently require this PR:
https://github.com/karma-runner/karma-googmodule-preprocessor/pull/23

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix(cesium): fix collection visibility

Cesium prefers wide scene trees to deep ones, but there are several
collection implementations that do not implement the 'show' property,
preventing us from setting the visibility at the collection level
(representing layer visibility). Therefore, these collections are added
under a root PrimitiveCollection so that it's 'show' property can be
used to properly control their visibility.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix(kml): miscellaneous ground overlay fixes

When parsing a ground overlay in a projection other than EPSG:4326, reproject the extent

appropriately. This may be unintended by the author of the KML and not the original projection of

the image, but the goal here is to 'do the best thing' that we can do. Converting the extent allows

Go To to work properly, and will make a best-effort attempt at showing the image. If we need to do

additional work later to follow our more strict reprojection rules for imagery layers, we can do

that. Also added fixes to multiple places reading the extent since we moved its location.

message:
fix(cesium): replace use of Cesium's camera.computeViewRectangle

because it is inaccurate in several ways. It only uses the corners
of the screen as sample points (4 compared to 64 now), and it also
gives up and assumes that the rectangle is Rectangle.MAX_VALUE
if at least 3 of those corners are in space (Rectangle.MAX_VALUE is
not ever a correct view rectangle because the camera can only see
roughly half the globe at once).

In order to fix (many) DeveloperErrors in Cesium, lines no longer always
use the same appearance, and rather only use the
PolylineMaterialAppearance when a dash is used in the style. This allows
for better performance in general, but now we need the
isDashPatternChanging() method to check that the dashPattern is not
defined (the correct value matching the else case of no
PolylineMaterialAppearance).

message:
fix(query): Only layers affected by entry changes should load

Previously, using a double-wildcard area to load features from multiple layers and then going into

one of those layers' filter GUIs to add an attribute filter would cause both layers to load on

Apply. Now, rather than merging the entries and always removing all and adding back in the merged

entries, we just remove the entries for the layerIds affected by the incoming entries. For the merge

case, the old entries for the revert are filtered from the full set. The non-merge case (all layer

advanced view) still removes/adds all.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
refactor(cesium): reorganize featureconverter

This is largely a reorganization, not a rewrite or a change in logic.
FeatureConverter was a spaghetti mess and hard to make sense of for
anyone outside of a couple of experts.

The general design for the refactor is shown in sync/convertertypes.js
and sync/runconverter.js. The individual converter implementations are
all pulled in by sync/converter.js.

This is largely an attempt at feature-parity with the previous
converter, with the following changes:

  - Several style bugs were fixed by consolidating and reusing
    style code where possible instead of using the previous one-off
    implementations
  - All functions being sent a feature, geometry, style, and context now
    have a consistent parameter order everywhere
  - A few minor performance items were added (typically things like
    using scratch arrays objects where possible)
  - All instances of @suppress {checkTypes} were removed and fixed
  - Most larger functions have been split into smaller blocks with a
    couple of exceptions.

I attempted to change anything outside of FeatureConverter the least
amount possible (VectorSynchronizer and VectorContext) other than
converting them to ES6 class syntax.

update those primitives and must instead recreate them.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix: fire event only after overridden getter ready

OL's obj.set(property, value) fires a `change:${property}` event
automatically. However, the OpenLayers event does not put the new value
on the event. Only the old value. Therefore, it is expected that a
listener for that event should be able to call the getter for that
property (in this case getSharpness or getBrightness, but also more
generically get(property)) and return the correct new value.

resolves #1046

message:
chore(hooks): prevent issue collisions between github and bitbucket

Our internal bitbucket server references "pull request #X in WV/..." in merge

commit messages, but it doesn't use the # to actually reference anything. The #X

reference is causing unrelated references in Github. Therefore, this hook

rewrites that commit message in a way that keeps all the information but does not

cause the unrelated references.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix(cesium): use Image rather than ImageIcon.load

Using the underlying OL style to load the icon is problematic because
ImageIcon applies color to the image. That's all well and good, but it
requires setting the imageId in Cesium to 'src + color' rather than just
'src', which blows up the texture atlas. The solution is just to load
the image directly and let Cesium color it. The downside is that custom
extensions of those icon classes will not work properly (we do not
currently have any).

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix(mixin): address ng isClass failures

ng isClass() used in invoke() is incorrect in that it does not
check func.hasOwnProperty('$$ngIsClass'). If an ES6 class extends
an older class structure, isClass() will report the parent's
cached result.

Example:
  const OldClass = function() {};
  OldClass.$$ngIsClass = false;
  class NewClass extends OldClass;
  NewClass.$$ngIsClass // false!

Therefore, this mixes in a fix for that in $injector.invoke just
after os.ui.injector is set in AbstractMainCtrl.

message:
fix(kml): miscellaneous ground overlay fixes

When parsing a ground overlay in a projection other than EPSG:4326, reproject the extent

appropriately. This may be unintended by the author of the KML and not the original projection of

the image, but the goal here is to 'do the best thing' that we can do. Converting the extent allows

Go To to work properly, and will make a best-effort attempt at showing the image. If we need to do

additional work later to follow our more strict reprojection rules for imagery layers, we can do

that. Also added fixes to multiple places reading the extent since we moved its location.

Previously, using a double-wildcard area to load features from multiple layers and then going into

one of those layers' filter GUIs to add an attribute filter would cause both layers to load on

Apply. Now, rather than merging the entries and always removing all and adding back in the merged

entries, we just remove the entries for the layerIds affected by the incoming entries. For the merge

case, the old entries for the revert are filtered from the full set. The non-merge case (all layer

advanced view) still removes/adds all.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
build(windows): fix font path in Windows

The old setup was only suitable if a project had a symlink from
project/vendor/fonts to opensphere/vendor/fonts. Symlinks do not
work in Windows.

Therefore, we use a well-defined path to opensphere within the
workspace.

Note that I do not believe that this method is compatible with
using opensphere as a library within node_modules. That will
need to be a follow-on for later investigation.

message:
perf(cesium): improved memory usage for points

Points using RegularShape styles now (potentially) use less memory by
keeping a single instance of the shape with a white fill, using the
'color' property of the billboard to color it. I say "potentially"
because the full memory usage is still occuring on the OL/StyleManager
side when the styles are created/updated. We could potentially add a
mixin loaded by the Cesium plugin which could disable that since the
billboards no longer need the original image style off of those.

comments. The code adds the real column definitions to the sort columns
returned by `slick.grid.getSortColumns()` to speed up the sorting
functions. That's been extracted to a function, preserving the
explaining comments.

given to the sorting functions. This definition includes the column
definitions added by the extracted function described above.

scale, and changing it on the instance to 1 will make all requests
for the original scale pull 1 instead.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix: fire event only after overridden getter ready

OL's obj.set(property, value) fires a `change:${property}` event
automatically. However, the OpenLayers event does not put the new value
on the event. Only the old value. Therefore, it is expected that a
listener for that event should be able to call the getter for that
property (in this case getSharpness or getBrightness, but also more
generically get(property)) and return the correct new value.

resolves #1046

There are some google maps icons which are not available for closed
network usage by duplicating them in images/icons/kml. Previously, any
file referencing those icons failed with a message in the console and
did not show the point. This addresses that issue by checking to see if
the icon is one of the ones that we enumerate for the google icon set.

Additionally, the KML plugin now checks if maps.google.com is accessible
and sets a flag that informs whether to use the default icon for missing
URLs or just use the URL directly.

message:
feat(filter-import): refactors filter import to work with layers and filterables

This changes the layerpicker directive to work with layers and both the filter and filter action import directives to
work with non-descriptor IFilterables. It also allows for more flexible choice of which layers your
filters go to on import rather than defaulting them to the specified type. It makes filters and
feature actions work on layers from state files and from regular files.

BREAKING CHANGE: changes the output of the filter/filteraction parsers, mucks with a few filter APIs

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix(mixin): address ng isClass failures

ng isClass() used in invoke() is incorrect in that it does not
check func.hasOwnProperty('$$ngIsClass'). If an ES6 class extends
an older class structure, isClass() will report the parent's
cached result.

Example:
  const OldClass = function() {};
  OldClass.$$ngIsClass = false;
  class NewClass extends OldClass;
  NewClass.$$ngIsClass // false!

Therefore, this mixes in a fix for that in $injector.invoke just
after os.ui.injector is set in AbstractMainCtrl.

style(bs): use margin-bottom from bootstrap

the bottom border from showing on the active tab in some situations. We override
margin for .nav-link, causing the bottom border to show. We only want to change
the left/right margin, so that is now done directly with margin-left and
margin-right.

author: MarcelloNicoletti <marcello.s.nicoletti@gmail.com>
message:
fix(CSVExport): Prevent hidden columns from being included in export

Geometry and time fields were always included in the export, even if their
columns were hidden. This commit adds an option to always ensure a WKT geometry
field is included. This option defaults to true. When this option is false the
geometry is only included when the column is visible. This commit also changes
the time field to be included soley based on column visibility.

BREAKING CHANGE: Previously all of the following fields were always included:
`LAT`, `LON`, `LAT_DMS`, `LON_DMS`, `LAT_DDS`, `LON_DDS`, `MGRS`, `GEOMETRY`,
and `TIME`. Now only the `GEOMETRY` field is included, and it contains a WKT
representation of the data. `TIME` is now only included based on visibility.

author: MarcelloNicoletti <marcello.s.nicoletti@gmail.com>
message:
fix(CSVExport): Prevent hidden columns from being included in export

Geometry and time fields were always included in the export, even if their
columns were hidden. This commit adds an option to always ensure a WKT geometry
field is included. This option defaults to true. When this option is false the
geometry is only included when the column is visible. This commit also changes
the time field to be included soley based on column visibility.

BREAKING CHANGE: Previously all of the following fields were always included:
`LAT`, `LON`, `LAT_DMS`, `LON_DMS`, `LAT_DDS`, `LON_DDS`, `MGRS`, `GEOMETRY`,
and `TIME`. Now only the `GEOMETRY` field is included, and it contains a WKT
representation of the data. `TIME` is now only included based on visibility.

message:
fix(cesium): hacky fix for some bugs in Cesium's explicit rendering

The old ol-cesium render loop fired rendering when Cesium's request
stack finished a request. This has been restored. Additionally,
when the render loop is fired via a GL_REPAINT event, the loop
continuously renders for a whole second at the target framerate
rather than simply rendering once. This covers the async load of
an icon and asynchronously loading it to the GPU.

THIN-11821

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix(net): credentials handler should not save results

Some servers provide error pages that are redirected and do not result in error code responses
(maintenance pages are also occasionally a problem if they do not return 503). Therefore,
CredentialsHandler should not save information because it can't really know if the request "worked"
outside of the status code.

THIN-11696

fix(kml): miscellaneous ground overlay fixes

When parsing a ground overlay in a projection other than EPSG:4326, reproject the extent

appropriately. This may be unintended by the author of the KML and not the original projection of

the image, but the goal here is to 'do the best thing' that we can do. Converting the extent allows

Go To to work properly, and will make a best-effort attempt at showing the image. If we need to do

additional work later to follow our more strict reprojection rules for imagery layers, we can do

that. Also added fixes to multiple places reading the extent since we moved its location.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix(cesium): fix collection visibility

Cesium prefers wide scene trees to deep ones, but there are several
collection implementations that do not implement the 'show' property,
preventing us from setting the visibility at the collection level
(representing layer visibility). Therefore, these collections are added
under a root PrimitiveCollection so that it's 'show' property can be
used to properly control their visibility.

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix(kml): fix missing google maps icons

There are some google maps icons which are not available for closed
network usage by duplicating them in images/icons/kml. Previously, any
file referencing those icons failed with a message in the console and
did not show the point. This addresses that issue by checking to see if
the icon is one of the ones that we enumerate for the google icon set.

Additionally, the KML plugin now checks if maps.google.com is accessible
and sets a flag that informs whether to use the default icon for missing
URLs or just use the URL directly.

message:
fix(cesium): use dash change detection

In order to fix (many) DeveloperErrors in Cesium, lines no longer always
use the same appearance, and rather only use the
PolylineMaterialAppearance when a dash is used in the style. This allows
for better performance in general, but now we need the
isDashPatternChanging() method to check that the dashPattern is not
defined (the correct value matching the else case of no
PolylineMaterialAppearance).

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix(kml): miscellaneous ground overlay fixes

When parsing a ground overlay in a projection other than EPSG:4326, reproject the extent

appropriately. This may be unintended by the author of the KML and not the original projection of

the image, but the goal here is to 'do the best thing' that we can do. Converting the extent allows

Go To to work properly, and will make a best-effort attempt at showing the image. If we need to do

additional work later to follow our more strict reprojection rules for imagery layers, we can do

that. Also added fixes to multiple places reading the extent since we moved its location.

fix(query): Only layers affected by entry changes should load

Previously, using a double-wildcard area to load features from multiple layers and then going into

one of those layers' filter GUIs to add an attribute filter would cause both layers to load on

Apply. Now, rather than merging the entries and always removing all and adding back in the merged

entries, we just remove the entries for the layerIds affected by the incoming entries. For the merge

case, the old entries for the revert are filtered from the full set. The non-merge case (all layer

advanced view) still removes/adds all.

has been left the same to avoid breaking its usage).

receiving end of these requests to code around that bug need to be reviewed and possibly removed.

parsing out domain names. Please use `new goog.Uri(str).getDomain() or `new URL(str).hostname`

author: William Wall <wwall@caci.com>
message:
fix(cesium): use Image rather than ImageIcon.load

Using the underlying OL style to load the icon is problematic because
ImageIcon applies color to the image. That's all well and good, but it
requires setting the imageId in Cesium to 'src + color' rather than just
'src', which blows up the texture atlas. The solution is just to load
the image directly and let Cesium color it. The downside is that custom
extensions of those icon classes will not work properly (we do not
currently have any).
